correctness.rationale: The actual 90-tetrahedron source and actual permutation/edge-generator certificate were inspected, not just its saved output. An independent exact evaluator reconstructed \(f=(16,106,180,90)\), the 411 three-cliques with 180 faces and 231 nonfaces, the BFS spanning tree with 91 chord generators, and all 180 relators. The 120-point permutations generate a group of order 120 and are actual images of two chord generators; every relator maps to the identity, so the resulting map of \(\pi_1\) is surjective. The established binary-icosahedral fundamental group has order 120, making it an isomorphism. Re-evaluation of all 231 missing triangles gave order 10 each, with a single size-12 conjugacy class containing its inverses. Facial loops bound triangles and simple graph cycles have length at least 3, proving the claimed complete combinatorial minimum. This is an exact finite exhaustive certificate with an explicit published topology premise, not an empirical inference.
residual_risks: The Björner--Lutz original full article could not be acquired through authorized sources during this run; the topological identification is corroborated by accessible library records.

value.rationale: The combinatorial systole and exact number/conjugacy type of shortest essential loops on a canonical asymmetric triangulation are natural homotopy invariants of the particular finite object. The size-12 inverse-stable concentration across 231 distinct carriers is not a textbook consequence of the global group and provides a concrete test case for short-loop topology computations.

final_claim: In the Björner--Lutz labelled sixteen-vertex triangulation of the Poincaré homology three-sphere, the simple noncontractible edge-loop systole is \(3\); exactly \(231\) missing three-cliques attain it, each maps to an element of order \(10\) in the binary icosahedral fundamental group, and all their images lie in one inverse-stable conjugacy class of size \(12\).
limitations: Only simple edge cycles of this labelled triangulation and combinatorial edge count, not arbitrary loops or Riemannian geodesics.
The group-isomorphism argument relies on the published identification of this triangulation with the Poincaré homology sphere and \(\lvert\pi_1\rvert=120\).
